clue.text: Permit to join in former generation's diversion

parts.note: the former generation is your father, Pa, so its possessive is Pa's
a sport is a pastime or diversion

explanation.surface: Permission to take part in the games one's father's generation enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: PA'S (the father's, the former generation's) is followed by SPORT (diversion); the apostrophe drops out in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the travel document that permits entry into a foreign country.

clue.text: Forward types might get cut ?

parts.note: rugby forwards collectively form a group, and the same word names a deck of cards, which players cut

explanation.surface: Pushy people may be snubbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Forward types' looks like pushy people; it means rugby forwards, while 'cut' is what is done to a deck of cards.
explanation.definitionFit: The rugby forwards are called the pack, and a pack of cards is cut before dealing.

clue.text: Way woman artist meets worker

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
Eve is the first woman in Genesis
Gustave Dore was a French illustrator and artist

explanation.surface: On the road a lady painter encounters a labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A stevedore is a dock labourer who loads and unloads ships.

clue.text: Excuse scholar being under standard

indicators.note: in a down clue, being under puts the scholar's word below the standard's

parts.note: par is the standard or norm
a don is a university teacher

explanation.surface: An academic is excused for falling below the norm.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon someone is to forgive or excuse them.

clue.text: Remainder live round the youth centre

indicators.note: round means the word for live is placed around the other letter

parts.note: to reside is to live somewhere

indicators.note: the centre of youth is its middle letter

explanation.surface: The rest dwell around the young people's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre' takes U, the middle letter of 'youth', and 'round' puts RESIDE around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A residue is what is left over, the remainder.

clue.text: Accept lift ?

explanation.surface: Take an offer of a ride.
explanation.definitionFit: To take up an offer is to accept it, and to take up a carpet or hem is to lift it.

clue.text: Perhaps helping wrong-doer as a matter of course

explanation.surface: Aiding a criminal routinely.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as A BETTING: on a race course a bet is a matter of course.
explanation.definitionFit: Abetting is assisting someone in a crime, as in aiding and abetting; a betting matter is what happens at a race course.

clue.text: Diminish, removing fifty in Germany

definitions.note: the definition names where the city lies, a place in Germany

indicators.note: removing tells you a letter comes out of the word for diminish

parts.note: to lessen is to diminish
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Cutting back, dropping fifty jobs in Germany.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in the Ruhr, in western Germany.

clue.text: Peter meant to take a different line

indicators.note: take a different form: the letters of Peter meant are rearranged

explanation.surface: Peter intended to adopt another approach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take a different' rearranges PETER MEANT; 'line' is the definition, not part of the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A pentameter is a line of verse with five metrical feet.

clue.text: Its reign 1793-1794

parts.note: the period of the French Revolution when mass executions ruled was known as the Reign of this

explanation.surface: A monarch's rule lasting a year.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reign of Terror was the period of the French Revolution marked by mass executions by guillotine.

clue.text: Many play, that's obvious

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, crossword shorthand for many
King Lear is Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A comment that lots of people perform a drama, which is self-evident.
explanation.definitionFit: Something plain and evident is easily seen, so obvious.

clue.text: Writer initially gets the right learners

definitions.text: Writer initially gets the right learners

parts.words: Writer initially gets the right learners
parts.note: read 'initially' as initials: a writer whose initials are R for right and L for learner, Robert Louis by name

explanation.surface: An author starts out by attracting the right students.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue builds nothing from letters: R (right) and L (learner) are the author's initials, R.L., pointing to the Treasure Island author.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson, author of Treasure Island and Kidnapped, has the initials R.L.

clue.text: Judge receives blow from player ?

explanation.surface: A magistrate is struck by a sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'blow' is a punch; in the second sense it is the breath a player blows into a wind instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: In England a recorder is a part-time criminal judge, and the recorder is a woodwind instrument the player blows into.

clue.text: Got another order for a native cart

indicators.note: read 'another' as 'an other', so 'other order' tells you to put the letters of Got and an into a different arrangement

parts.note: split as 'an other': its first word an joins the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone received a further command about a local cart.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'another' as 'an other': 'other order' rearranges GOT + AN into TONGA.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonga is a light two-wheeled horse-drawn cart used in India.

clue.text: Measure for obtaining more milk — a new scheme round Gateshead

indicators.note: round means the rearranged letters go around the single letter
a new scheme for the letters of more milk and a means arranging them afresh

parts.note: read as Gate's head, the first letter of gate, G

explanation.surface: A plan for Gateshead aimed at getting more milk produced.
explanation.walkthrough: Read Gateshead (a town in north-east England) as Gate's head, G. 'new scheme' rearranges MORE MILK A into KILORAMME, and 'round' puts it around G.
explanation.definitionFit: A kilogramme is a unit of weight, a thousand grams.

clue.text: Press club

explanation.surface: A newspaper association.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a journalists' club; both words are separate senses.
explanation.definitionFit: To press clothes is to smooth them with a hot appliance, and in golf an iron is a metal-headed club.

clue.text: Drawer behind the counter, perhaps

parts.note: a drawer here is something that draws, a pump that pulls ale up from the cellar to the bar

explanation.surface: A till drawer kept beneath a shop counter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' looks like a sliding box under a shop counter; it is something that draws ale behind a pub bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A beer-engine is the hand pump on a pub bar that draws ale up from the cellar.

clue.text: Content with average time ?'

indicators.note: the content of a word is what lies inside it, so the letters sit within average

explanation.surface: Satisfied with an ordinary duration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like 'satisfied'; read it as 'contents', the letters inside 'average'.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of time.

clue.text: New oil-rig mob gets into a tangle

indicators.note: new tells you to make a new arrangement of the letters of oil-rig mob

explanation.surface: A freshly arrived gang at a drilling platform get into a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' rearranges OILRIG MOB.
explanation.definitionFit: An imbroglio is a confused and complicated situation, a tangle.

clue.text: Space traveller makes a bloomer? Nothing I'd conclude

indicators.note: conclude says the last piece, I'd, comes at the end

parts.note: a bloomer is a flowering plant, here the aster
O is zero, nothing
taken as its letters

explanation.surface: An astronaut blunders; I would decide it was nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flower, ASTER.
explanation.definitionFit: An asteroid is a small rocky body orbiting the sun, travelling through space.

clue.text: Spell words from an oriental tale

explanation.surface: An incantation quoted from an Eastern story.
explanation.definitionFit: The magic password in Ali Baba and the Forty Thieves, from the Arabian Nights, opens the robbers' cave.

clue.text: She'd lose nothing in a shipwreck

definitions.note: the definition is a woman's name, a she

indicators.note: in tells you a letter goes inside the rearranged letters
wreck means the letters of a ship are smashed up and rearranged

parts.note: O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A woman who would come out of a shipwreck unscathed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wreck' rearranges A SHIP into SPHIA, and 'in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia is a woman's given name, Greek for wisdom.

clue.text: Reverenced by the brave ?

parts.note: a brave is a Native American warrior, and this is the spirit such warriors revered

explanation.surface: Something the courageous hold in awe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the brave' looks like courageous people; it is a Native American warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Manitou is the Algonquian name for a supernatural spirit or power worshipped by Native Americans.

clue.text: Music maker sounds like a tramp, doesn't 'e ?

indicators.note: these words say the instrument's name is pronounced like the Cockney word that follows

parts.note: a tramp is a hobo, and the Cockney tag 'doesn't 'e' drops the h, leaving 'obo

explanation.surface: An instrument that sounds like a down-and-out, wouldn't you agree?
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney drops the H from HOBO, and 'obo sounds like the woodwind; 'doesn't 'e' shows the dropped H.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a double-reed woodwind instrument, a maker of music.

clue.text: Notoriously ignorant, yet looks down on everyone

definitions.text: Notoriously ignorant, yet looks down on everyone

parts.words: Notoriously ignorant, yet looks down on everyone
parts.note: the face seen ... lunar disc knows nothing, as the saying goes, yet gazes down on all of us from the sky

explanation.surface: A famously stupid snob who despises everybody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looks down on' looks like snobbery; it is literal, from the sky. 'To know no more than the man in the moon' is a saying for total ignorance.
explanation.definitionFit: The face seen on the full moon is proverbially ignorant, as in knowing no more than it does.

clue.text: Lift beams, say ?

indicators.note: 'say' asks you to hear the previous word spoken

parts.note: beams of light are rays

explanation.surface: Hoist the girders, for example.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something is to hoist it higher.

clue.text: See 24
Cask for the liquor one brewed

parts.note: punch is a mixed alcoholic drink

indicators.note: brewed means the letters of one are mixed up as in a brew

explanation.surface: A barrel to hold the drink someone has made.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brewed' rearranges ONE into EON, after PUNCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A puncheon is a large barrel for wine or spirits.

clue.text: See 24
In a way, it's unusual for a religious person

parts.note: a method is a way of doing something

indicators.note: unusual tells you the letters of it's are put out of their normal order

parts.note: taken as its letters

explanation.surface: Somehow it is odd for a person of faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ITS into IST, after METHOD.
explanation.definitionFit: A Methodist belongs to the Protestant denomination founded by John Wesley.

clue.text: Port of use in dismal moments ?

indicators.note: in shows the port's name is contained in the words dismal moments

explanation.surface: A harbour useful in gloomy times.
explanation.definitionFit: Malmo is a Swedish port on the Oresund.

clue.text: Improves what tinker does, as Cockney says

indicators.note: a Cockney drops the h, so the phrase is pronounced as he would say it

parts.note: a tinker mends pots, so 'he mends' describes what he does

explanation.surface: A Londoner explains that a travelling repairman makes things better.
explanation.walkthrough: A tinker is a travelling mender of pots and pans; 'he mends' with the H dropped becomes 'e mends.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend a text is to correct and so improve it.

clue.text: Reject this collar ?

explanation.surface: Refuse to wear this neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: To turn down an offer is to reject it, and a turndown is a collar folded over at the neck.
